inline.s: [The Buddha told Ananda: You must hold well to these words! Whoever holds to these words is thereby holding the name of the Buddha of Immeasurable Life.]
The Buddha told Ananda: You must receive and hold well to this scripture that I have now preached! To receive and hold to this scripture is to hold and recite the name of Amitabha Buddha.
This passage is the Buddha answering Ananda’s question in the text above: What is the essential of this Dharma, and how should it be received and held?
Master Shandao, in his Commentary on the Four Sections of the Contemplation Sutra, says:

“From the words ‘the Buddha told Ananda, you must hold well to these words’ onward, it precisely shows that the name of Amitabha was entrusted to [Ananda] to be spread abroad through distant ages. Although the foregoing set forth the benefits of the two gates of meditative and non-meditative practice, yet having regard to the Buddha’s original vow, the intent is that beings should single-mindedly and exclusively recite the name of Amitabha Buddha.”

(Translation: This passage of scripture — “The Buddha told Ananda: you must hold well to these words! Whoever holds to these words is thereby holding the name of the Buddha of Immeasurable Life” — precisely shows that the World-honored One entrusted Ananda with the practice of name-recitation (reciting the name of Amitabha Buddha) to be spread down to distant posterity. Although the scriptures above expounded the benefits of the two gates of meditative and non-meditative practice, yet having regard to the fundamental vow of Shakyamuni Buddha, the intent is that beings should exclusively and single-mindedly recite the name of Amitabha Buddha.)

[The two gates of meditative and non-meditative practice: In his Commentary on the Four Sections of the Contemplation Sutra, Master Shandao divides the sixteen contemplations into the two gates of meditative virtue and non-meditative virtue. The first thirteen contemplations (from the sun contemplation to the miscellaneous contemplation) use a mind of meditative concentration to contemplate the dependent and primary retributions of the Land of Ultimate Bliss, and so are called ‘meditative virtue’; the last three contemplations practice the three grades [of virtue] and nine grades [of birth] through a non-meditative mind, and so are called ‘non-meditative virtue.’] [Exclusively and single-mindedly reciting the name of Amitabha Buddha: this is the ‘single-minded exclusive recitation’ spoken of in the Immeasurable Life Sutra — to be forever single-mindedly holding the name and reciting the Buddha, with no other thoughts. [When the Buddha spoke these words, the Venerable Maudgalyayana, the Venerable Ananda, and Vaidehi and the others, having heard what the Buddha said, were all filled with great joy.]

When the World-honored One had finished preaching this scripture, the Venerable Maudgalyayana, the Venerable Ananda, and Vaidehi and the others, having heard what the Buddha said, were all filled with great joy.
The above is the World-honored One, while in the palace of confinement, teaching the Dharma to Vaidehi and the others.
The following is the Venerable Ananda, on Vulture Peak, proclaiming this scripture on behalf of the Buddha to the holy assembly.
[At that time, the World-honored One, treading through the sky, returned to Vulture Peak.]
At that time, the World-honored One, treading the sky, returned to Vulture Peak.

[At that time, Ananda widely proclaimed the above matters to the great assembly. The countless gods, nagas, and yakshas, having heard what the Buddha said, were all filled with great joy, and after paying homage to the Buddha withdrew.]

At that time, the Venerable Ananda widely proclaimed the above matters to the great assembly (the great assembly of bhikshus numbering one thousand two hundred and fifty, the thirty-two thousand bodhisattvas, and the bodhisattva Manjushri at their head). The countless gods, nagas, and yakshas, having heard this scripture spoken by the Buddha, were all filled with great joy, and after paying homage to the Buddha withdrew.
